proof:
Source: steps 6(a)–(b) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2, lines 2117–2124: "by 3.13 we can define integer multiplicity R^{(ℓ)}, S^{(ℓ)} by the M-absolutely convergent series"), and Simon's Lemma 3.13 with its printed proof (chapter-06.txt lines 897–937), here with U = ℝ^P and the global mass M = M_{ℝ^P}.
Notation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞, with |·| the Euclidean coefficient norm. Hᵈ := μHE[d]. Siblings used: (IC) cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (a), (c); (MM) dtc_mass_eq_measure; (VO) dtc_vanish_off_support.

1. (Evaluation bound.) For a current X with M(X) < ∞ and any ω, |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(X). If ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0, because |α| = 0 forces all coefficients α(e_I) (I increasing) to vanish and these determine α; then X(ω) = 0. Otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ are admissible for M, so ±X(ω) ≤ ‖ω‖M(X).
2. (Pointwise sum.) Let s := Σ_i M(X_i) < ∞; then every M(X_i) < ∞. For each ω, Σ_i |X_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖s < ∞, so Σ_i X_i(ω) converges absolutely. Let Y(ω) be its sum; then HasSum (i ↦ X_i(ω)) (Y(ω)).
3. (Y is a current.) Y is linear, as a sum of linear functionals. Continuity in Simon's sequential sense (6.2.1): suppose ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), i.e. the supports lie in a fixed compact set and all derivatives tend to 0 uniformly. Then sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖_op → 0. Also |α| ≤ (number of increasing I)^{1/2}·‖α‖_op, since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖_op. So ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and |Y(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖s → 0.
4. (Mass.) For admissible ω, ofReal Y(ω) = ofReal(Σ_i X_i(ω)) ≤ Σ_i ofReal X_i(ω) ≤ Σ_i M(X_i), because ofReal is subadditive and continuous. Taking the supremum, M(Y) ≤ s. The same argument applied to a tail series gives M(Y − Σ_{i<N} X_i) ≤ Σ_{i≥N} M(X_i).
5. (Support.) Let F := closure(⋃_i spt X_i) and x ∉ F, and choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ∩ F = ∅. If tsupport ω ⊆ B_r(x), then tsupport ω is disjoint from every spt X_i, so X_i(ω) = 0 by (VO) and Y(ω) = 0. B_r(x) is open with compact closure, so it is one of the sets whose union is the zero region of Y. Hence x ∉ spt Y, and spt Y ⊆ F.
6. (Integer multiplicity: Simon 3.13.) Assume every X_i is integer multiplicity.
 (a) The partial sums Z_N := X_0 + ⋯ + X_{N−1} are integer multiplicity. By (IC)(c), 0 = B − B, −B = 0 − B and A + B = A − (−B) are integer multiplicity whenever A and B are. By step 4, M(Y − Z_N) ≤ Σ_{i≥N} M(X_i) → 0. In particular (Z_N) is Cauchy for M.
 (b) Write Z_N = τ(M_N, θ_N, ξ_N), with θ_N := 0 and ξ_N := 0 off M_N. Let N ≤ N'. On M_N ∩ M_{N'} the approximate tangent spaces of M_N and M_{N'} agree Hᵈ-a.e. by (IC)(a), so ξ_{N'} = ±ξ_N there. Z_{N'} − Z_N is represented as in the construction of (IC)(c): multiplicity |θ_{N'} ∓ θ_N| on the overlap and θ_{N'}, resp. θ_N, off it. Its weight is |θ_{N'}ξ_{N'} − θ_Nξ_N|Hᵈ, where |aζ| = |a| for a unit simple d-vector ζ. So by (MM), M(Z_{N'} − Z_N) = ∫|θ_{N'}ξ_{N'} − θ_Nξ_N| dHᵈ =: ε(N, N'); this is Simon's (1). By (a), ε(N, N') → 0 as N → ∞, uniformly in N' ≥ N.
 (c) Since |ξ_N| = 1 on M_N and θ_N ≥ 0, ∫|θ_{N'} − θ_N| dHᵈ ≤ ε(N, N') (Simon's (2)). So θ_N → θ in L¹(Hᵈ) for some θ. A subsequence converges Hᵈ-a.e., so θ is integer valued with θ ≥ 0. Put M_+ := {θ > 0}. Since |θ_N − θ| ≥ 1 on (M_+ ∖ M_N) ∪ (M_N ∖ M_+), we get Hᵈ((M_+ ∖ M_N) ∪ (M_N ∖ M_+)) ≤ ∫|θ_N − θ| dHᵈ → 0 (Simon's (3)). In particular M_+ lies in ⋃_N M_N up to an Hᵈ-null set, so it is countably d-rectifiable, and ∫_{M_+} θ dHᵈ < ∞.
 (d) From (b) and (c), ∫θ_{N'}|ξ_{N'} − ξ_N| dHᵈ ≤ 2ε(N, N'). So ξ_N converges in L¹(Hᵈ⌞M_+) to a function ξ that is simple with |ξ| = 1 on M_+. By (c) and (IC)(a), T_xM_+ = T_xM_N for x ∈ M_+ outside a set whose measure tends to 0, and ξ_N(x) orients T_xM_N. Hence ξ(x) orients T_xM_+ for Hᵈ-a.e. x ∈ M_+, and Y' := τ(M_+, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity current.
 (e) M(Z_N − Y') ≤ ∫|θ_Nξ_N − θξ| dHᵈ → 0 (Simon: "M_W(T_P − T) → 0"). Both Y and Y' are limits of Z_N in mass, hence weakly, so Y = Y'. Thus Y is integer multiplicity. ∎
key_steps: |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖M(X), so Σ X_i(ω) converges absolutely; Y(ω) := Σ X_i(ω) is linear and sequentially continuous, so it is a current.
M(Y) ≤ Σ M(X_i), and spt Y ⊆ closure(⋃ spt X_i) because each X_i vanishes on forms supported off its support.
If the X_i are integer multiplicity, the partial sums Z_N are integer multiplicity and M(Y − Z_N) → 0.
Simon 3.13: θ_Nξ_N is Cauchy in L¹(Hᵈ); θ_N → θ integer valued, the carriers converge, ξ_N → ξ orients T_xM_+; so Y = τ(M_+, θ, ξ).
